correctness.rationale: Normalize a0=a1=1 by scalar and argument rotation, leaving u,v∈T. Fourier orthogonality yields coefficient square sum of P^k. Every exponent from (1+x+uy+vxy)^3 is mi+j with i,j≤3; m≥4 has no non-formal collisions, while m=3 has only (i,3)=(i+1,0) for i=0,1,2. Exact Laurent coefficients give M4=28+8cosφ, M6=256+144cosφ for m≥4 and M6=256+144cosφ+6(3+2cosφ)cosψ at m=3, φ=arg u-arg v, ψ=2arg u-arg v. Nonnegative deficits yield sharp minima/maxima and their unique m3 equality points; connected phase torus guarantees full intervals. Independent integer-Laurent convolution for m=3,4,5 agreed with these equations. Infinite m proof rests on collision bound, not finite tests.
